# Phillips

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P40](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0040), [v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolmaster at Avonlea school  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c15 P56](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0056), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr. Phillips  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P40](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0040)</sub>; Master  <sub>[v1 c15 P58](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0058)</sub>; Teddy Phillips  <sub>[v1 c18 P6](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0006)</sub>

## Personality

Mr. Phillips is sarcastic, strict, and prone to public humiliation as a form of punishment, though his attempts at order are erratic and short-lived. He frequently neglects his younger students to focus his attention on older pupils or personal distractions. Despite his harsh demeanor in the classroom, he demonstrates a romantic side through verse-writing and displays sentimentality during public recitations or farewells.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046), [v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c15 P60](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0060), [v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_

## History

Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he was known for maintaining a poor standard of discipline while devoting his energy primarily to preparing his oldest scholars for Queen's Academy. During his tenure, he openly courted one of his older pupils, Prissy Andrews, frequently helping her with lessons and bestowing gifts on her. In class, he frequently used public discipline, such as forcing Anne Shirley to stand at the blackboard with her name misspelled or compelling her to sit on the boys' side next to Gilbert Blythe. At a local evening concert, he performed Mark Antony's oration over the dead body of Caesar. At the end of June, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to his students upon his departure from Avonlea school, leaving several pupils in tears.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046), [v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v1 c21 P0](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0000), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)_

## Background by volume

- Boarded at Eben Wright's house during his time in Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c15 P56](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0056)</sub>
- Secured his position as Avonlea school teacher because his uncle was a school trustee  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
